efp.title: Orryx Implementation of Multimodal User Interface (MUI) Framework

content.p: The backbone of the MUI Framework would be supported by the Ferricia Engine, with Simple DirectMedia Layer (SDL) 3, OpenAL Soft and various graphics backends. Different parts play different roles in MUI for the complete UI architecture. Thus, the interoperation of the Engine library and the Kotlin interface becomes essential that should be efficient and effective. In this framework, the Abstract Graphical Interface Model (AGIM) would also be introduced, as the fundamental graphical system for the Engine's utilization. This Framework is only applicable to client targets but not dedicated server targets.

AGIM is responsible mostly for the GUI, by communicating with SDL and OpenGL. The AUI communicates with OpenAL for audio processing and output. If there is a Game Controller connected, the HUI may communicate with it via SDL. All other KUI responsibilities are also by communicating with SDL, partially handled by the AGIM System.

The entire backend of the MUI Framework would be included in the Engine by interoperating with the native libraries within it. Its responsibilities consist of window management, rendering, audio processing, input management, user feedback management and interactive simulations. Rendering would mostly be handled with only a single canvas on only a single window as a single viewport; audio processing and simulations would mostly be handled using OpenAL with sources transmitted via networking or resource management; other elements would mostly be handled using other SDL subsystems.

macOS enforces that all window-related tasks, including windowing, rendering and input events, to be handled in the main thread. Therefore, the main thread would do all windowing, rendering and primary raw event handling, with other tasks delegated to other threads. This should ensure the application could work on every target platform while only minimally allocating the main thread for all essential tasks. Meanwhile, this does not include any audio-related task.

Primary raw events include any raw pointer and key inputs, all window events sent by SDL. Most events would then be sent to AGIM Screen for event handling and processing in the GMS ticking thread. It is important to note that the objects and states in the GMS must be carefully handled so that they could be rendered in the main thread asynchronously safely.

In order to communicate with UIDs in MUI with standardized protocols, there must be defined sets of protocols for interactions and interoperability. This includes having standard protocols to interact with input devices, for various generic types of input devices.

Input devices include pointing devices, keying devices, gamepads, joysticks, etc. Basic input control schemes for Interactions on Screens and Menus would be: Baseline, keying devices only; and, Hybrid, combo of keying devices and pointing devices. Extensive schemes may configure input devices even further, like using relative or absolute pointing devices for different types of input controls. Gameplay input control schemes may be based on the above configurations. In order to ensure certain usability and controllability when primary input devices are not available, fallback schemes should be configured, or else users may have to edit configurations outside the application. Also, application should not assume that a keyboard must be available at any time in the system levels.

Pointing devices are a class of input devices. They include mice, trackballs, touchpads, touch screens, pointing sticks, pen tablets, etc. Standardized protocols to interact with certain behavior patterns of input controls shall be defined. However, eligible pointing equipment with at least two axes (type of axes depends on scheme) and two main buttons must be available; without eligible equipment, this may be unavailable, though it may be a combination of multiple devices. Also, for the main buttons, while two main buttons are necessary, other buttons must be considered assistive or optional, or otherwise such controls may not be accessible in common setups.

All the primary raw events are sent by or as a part of the SDL functionalities. It is important to note that there exist several event types that would never be used in the Engine. Also, custom user events would not be handled in SDL, but mostly in the Kotlin interface, so events like SDL_UserEvent and SDL_QuitEvent are not used. Since touchscreen, camera and pen are not the target devices to support, their corresponding events are also not used.

Since mobile platforms are not targetted, events primarily designed for mobile platforms are also ignored. However, the mechanism to notify the user through an application warning notification about the system or the heap is running low on memory is possible. Still, it is expected that the application is always optimized at a certain degree that it can still run and proceed properly without overly optimizing any important resources. When the application is low on memory, the user is responsible to manage memory size and reduce memory demands as much as possible depending on the customization configurations; otherwise, there is nothing the application could do to free up memory.

The application window could optionally reduce rendering frequency when the window is not active. This includes the conditions when the window is hidden, minimized, or occluded. The maximum number of frames per second (FPS) could be limited at 30 or the half of the display refresh rate. At any time, the window cannot render properly and should stop rendering when the window bounds are out of a single display area; spanning the window to multiple displays is currently an unsupported behavior for behavior correctness and validity. This means functions such as SDL_GetDisplayForWindow are not supported.

The application does not rely on system theme but its own textures and themes, so the event of system theme change is not used; the application might use system locale settings to identify which language to use when the game data directory is first initialized, but the value would not change afterward, so the event of system locale change is also not used.

Display events may be used only when the application is in fullscreen, but only for the events related to the display the window is rendered on. Otherwise, there is no need to take care of display information. However, when the window is moved or resized, the display and window states must be checked to see whether the window can still be rendered. It is important to note that the controls of rendering are still handled in the Kotlin interface, so the events must be forwarded to the Kotlin side.

When the window gained focus, it is assumed that all input device states are all "zero", meaning that all states are cleared or reset to origin. However, this must not always be true, so when the events of resetting states are fired but the states were already "zero", the states remain unchanged, but with warnings (recovered situations) emitted. It is important to note that the set of states in SDL is not used due to this reason. Also, when the window loses focus, all the input device states in the application should be reset to origin and never get updated until the window regains focus. When the cursor is out of the canvas's boundaries, the cursor is not regarded as focussing on the canvas, and the mouse events are not processed until the cursor enters the canvas's region again; the cursor becomes non-existed in the application and hidden in canvas when the cursor is not in the canvas's region.

Event timestamps are ignored. When they are polled from the SDL event queue, it is expected that they are sorted in chronological order, so the timestamps should not be enough to affect the synchronization states while they are pumped and polled per frame update.

The modifier key states in SDL are not used generally. For text typing, this should normally already be handled by the input editor, which is processed in other events such as text editing or text input. This includes key repeating, which is likely fired by the device or system. The application itself internally holds a set of key states updated by all the primary raw events, but not the keyboard states queried directly. Also, the game is not playable with an external on-screen keyboard tool.

Scancodes of the keys would always be used internally, but the keycodes may be used to display the hotkey settings in the application. Therefore, the keycodes in the events are ignored, but for displaying the key to users, a different way would be done. Since scancodes do not change on keyboard layouts, the users have to identify what layouts their keyboards are. This cannot simply be done by SDL functions as some keys may be undistinguishable (for keycodes) or not mapped against layouts between different keyboards (for scancodes). A custom-built layout key mappings could be done to correctly map the keys by user's choice, which is by default QWERTY. It is still a question whether SDL_GetKeyFromScancode could be used safely across different platforms and various devices.

There would be two modes for mouse or cursor inputs. By default, system cursor states are tracked and updated to cursor states, which means the cursor motion states are updated each tick to correspond to the cursor position retrieved from SDL. When the game is in gameplay, the cursor mode turns to relative and wraps the cursor in the window, most likely only at the center of the canvas. In this mode, the mouse motion events from SDL are used instead of tracing system cursor position.

It is possible to select keyboard and mouse devices to use to exclusively only accept the input events from just one device instead of all. However, by default, all keyboard and mouse devices would be accepted to allow further customization depending on this. There is a possible concern about the application may become unusable when the devices become unusable although other devices could still control the system, so this feature might be reserved.

Joystick and gamepad update completion events (SDL_EVENT_JOYSTICK_UPDATE_COMPLETE and SDL_EVENT_GAMEPAD_UPDATE_COMPLETE) are generally not used, since the status updates are done through polling all the events in the certain frame. If any issue has been encountered, such as unideal non-synchronization scenarios or delayed events, this should be reconsidered.

The AGIM would only be implemented in the Kryon layer with abstractions. Under AGIM, all AGIM Objects (AGIMOs) serve as graphical wrappers of the underlying objects they manage, such as data, states, even other AGIMOs. The hierarchy of AGIMOs includes Screens, Menus and Components, where one includes the next directly possibly without skipping any stratum. Rendering of them would be backed by the Engine's rendering system, using the low level Kotlin bindings. However, other aspects of MUI triggered by AGIMOs cannot be managed by AGIMOs but dedicated interface managers in MUI out of AGIM.

The ScreenManager manages Screens stored in a linked list, with one on the top covers the others underneath. The Screen on the top also blocks user interactions via GUI. In the rendering system, the RenderSystem renders the Screens managed by the ScreenManager onto the Canvas backed by the Engine.

Rendering of content is not affected by system's display scale; the application itself would include a GUI scale setting to scale the sizes of Menus and Components. However, this only affects the dimensions but not all the margins. In the implementation, margins would most likely use percentages or ratios. Still, the details of implementation about GUI scaling are still subject to confirmation.

It is complex to query the window safe area for rendering when it varies device by device. Therefore, it should always assume that the safe area would generally be the canvas area with paddings of 10 pixels, to make sure the rendering behavior is consistent enough across platforms. This only applied to important interactable or rendered content, general displayed content like the background, miscellaneous margins, paddings and borders are not affected by this.

Most graphical elements should be based on textures and the default shaders used with textures. Only if certain geometric shapes are really required, like dynamic or variable lines and curves used to show interactions and associate interactive elements on the GUI, the restriction to use only textures could be bypassed. However, it is still recommended to use customizable properties like colors via resources. In this case, the default shaders which take textures would not be used, but the shaders that take other attributes.

Styles of AGIMOs shall be handled via Abstract Style Description (ASD). Layouts of AGIMOs shall follow the styles specified, without any fallback to fail fast. However, several attributes may still have default values assigned even there is no ASD Rules.

In sources, ASD would be presented in binary formats provided by modules or embedded files. Although in some aspects, ASD is similar to CSS, but there are significant differences. From binary, ASD has to be parsed in the Engine and then presented to Kyon side.

When compared with CSS, there are several features that are not supported. Geometric decorators may not be greatly supported, but textures. Margins in ASD are not always available, possibly prohibited, but in another sense. Overflowing is strictly prohibited for simplicity and structural safety. Stacking and layering as in CSS are not implemented. Inheritance and Cascading as in CSS are very different.

Main uses of ASD include spacing, sizing, positioning, alignment, layout, images, textures, patterns and geometries, where animation or transition at the moment is still in consideration. It is possible that animation or transition may be implemented as keyframes or microprogramming.
There are several design principles with ASD:

list.li: No guarantee in forward or backward compatibility. Contents must only support the Version it specified.
Complementary to structured documents. ASD complements structured Contents, providing stylistic information. It should be easy to change the ASD with little or no impact on the Contents.
Flexibility. The key feature is the ability to cascade and abstract style information in levels and modules.
Abstract and non-linearity. As in characteristics of being abstract, style information may not be sequential nor always available.

Strict. Parsing of malformed ASD shall fail fast to prevent using non-conformant style information and overly complicated handling of complex styles. This may also avoid misinterpretation of unsupported combinations of values.

content.p: To incorporate into AGIM, there are a few special features. ASD Properties are often constrained and limited in various conditions largely depending on structures and applied style information, and may sometimes be computed from cascading style information or others by certain specified processors and types. ASD is strict about Content Structures, and thus CSS features like pseudo-elements and pseudo-classes are not compatible with AGIM System, unless certain Contents are formed from Components (potentially with Secondary Selectors) that could be identified via Selectors and controlled by ASD. Everything in ASD is block-level in the sense of CSS, text formatting is separately handled, although overall formatting can still be specified in ASD of text-related Components.

Like CSS, there are Selectors in ASD, and ASD Entries may be nested for certain structures, but a few Selectors shall be prohibited. However, cascading rules are very different. For each Entry, there may be Priorities, without any specificity. There is also no inheritance of Properties, but other Entries can be referenced. Other than assigned Priorities, sequences of Entries and modules are also considered. This may also reduce opportunities abusing or flooding Rules to irrelevant Subjects, reducing sizes of Lists of Rules for Subjects while increasing accuracy of Subjects; Authors are expected to tend to narrower Selectors to avoid overriding Rules on unintended Subjects.

A Primary Selector consists of a Selector List of Primary Selector Entries, which specify for Primary Selector Subjects. A Primary Selector Subject consists of a class name, an assigned identifier (if any) and a Primary Attribute Selector, where only one or more of them can be specified. A Secondary Selector specify Facet(s) of Primary Subjects, by an Identifier of Layout Element in the Layout, an assigned identifier (if any) and a Secondary Attribute Selector, where only one or more of them can be specified.

A Selector List (Group) consists of Selector Entries with operators. General operators include OR, ADJ LOSSY, DES LOSSY, ADJ CLOSE, DES CLOSE. Special operators include NAME-ID, ID-NAME, NAME-ATTR, ATTR-NAME, ID-ATTR, ATTR-ID. Special Operators shall be specified only when Left and Right entries match the values; they operate as AND, and either side could be a List with only the specified type. For each entry in a List, a Selector shall present.

For values of Selectors, there are special meanings. All NULL shall match any Subject. Class Name may be a fully qualified name (FQN) of Java Class for an AGIMO. ID shall match any Subject with an assigned identifier equal to the value

For Selector Attributes, Ordinary Attributes are the Attributes that AGIMOs (Subjects) shall process, identify and filter against; Special Attributes are the Attributes that ASD Processors process, identify and filter against. Special Selector Attributes include FIRST CHILD, HOVER, ACTIVE, FOCUS.

When a Property is not assigned, it shall likely be unset and thus not making any effect. However, there may be required Properties that must be set by any ASD Rules; absence of such Properties likely results in failures instead of fallbacks or initial values. Usually, a Property declaration should be allowed to refer to another value or declaration with a syntax, or inherit declarations with certain positions.

Type 0 and Type 1 Values may initiate errors if the Property or Subjects do not allow, or an actual value cannot be fetched by any means. In Type 1, cyclic relationships shall not be allowed. Type 0 is DEFAULT, the default value of the Property; not all Properties must be with initial values definitely defined. Type 1 is REFERENCE, reference to another Property declaration for the value computed. In Type 1, there are several types of parameters, including ANCESTOR, BASE, LOCAL, FOREIGN. Type 2 is DEFINITE, a definite value is to be specified.

In ASD, backgrounds, textures and images can be specified, where there may also be Image Patterns for usage of advanced tiling or forms of images. They can be declared in variables or embedded in place of Property declarations. References to an image resource by a Resource Location can be specified. If in formatted images, references with URL links are used, they shall be resolved in a way that can be resolved with Resource Location; this part shall be resolved in its dedicated section.

Geometric patterns may be specified (to be used in borders), like stroke dashes can be specified, as in SVG stroke-dasharray. However, this may either be implemented with our own format or utilizing existing formats.

Instead of sophisticated microprogramming via a programming language, an embedded SVG (or another mature format) may be recommended. So in SVG, a <pattern> can be used to specify a pattern to be used for this ASD entry, by a pattern ID specified along with the formatted image. Moreover, unit resolution is also a part that worth noticing as units in those images are most likely different from the way used in AGIM System and ASD.

Cascading Rules in ASD differ from CSS, only a few factors are considered. Most inheritance of values are handled via declaration references. Other than this, there are also Priorities and Sequences, where Priorities have the highest precedence of cascading. Although Priorities may not be ideal, but should be useful for styles in end products, and this is rather suggestive, that Priorities may eventually be not useful.
Unassigned Priority shall be given a Base Priority, which has a lower priority than those with a Priority assigned. In format, Priorities are Unsigned VarInt.

There are two kinds of sequences: Sequence of ASD entries in a single module, and Sequence of modules (possibly with their own priorities) of ASD. The later or higher entries get the higher precedence.

This may also reduce opportunities abusing or flooding Rules to irrelevant Subjects, reducing sizes of Lists of Rules for Subjects. Authors are expected to tend to narrower Selectors to avoid overriding Rules on unintended Subjects.
All resources referred and used by ASD must present locally, for the ability to execute without connection to the Internet, and security in any aspect.

ASD shall also format and style certain media like images and videos, with special Properties and Components for the Contents. Those may consider intrinsic (or natural) dimensions of the media, while those dimensions may be either static or dynamic depending on the situations. It is also possible that those media do not provide intrinsic information about certain media contents.

Any values in ASD must not be ignored and must be processed by any means. For unknown or unsupported values, errors or warnings (if suppressed) must be emitted, unless the expectation is by an extension, which shall inject handlers into the processors.
Certain Properties may be Parameterized Enums or conditionally illegal depending on states of any related values, so legal values of those Properties may not be static.

Certain values are regarded as fractions or ratios, as a proportion of a reference dimension with a specified scale. Those specified values in declarations may be (with a byte for data type) floats, posits, fractions (fixed or varint), integers, Stern-Brocot rationals, etc., but procedures of processors must accurately compute without losing precision and information, so algorithms may differ for different data types. Integer-only Properties may likely use VarInt (LED128 with StreamVByte) for flexibility.
Comments may be enabled in Headers, but it is recommended to disable comments in production. When comments are enabled, certain places may accept optional comments or NULL.

There are Relative Units and Absolute Units. Relative Units must require and may adapt upon contexts for the applied Component. Absolute Units are constant in a state of application environment. Physical measurements of devices shall not be directly considered. There are several Graphical Units for Numeric Values:

list.li: By font size (relative): each unit equals to the font size; VAT may display it as "em".
By a half of font size (relative): each unit equals to a half of the font size; VAT may display it as "en".
By lowest recommended font size (relative): each unit equals to the lowest recommended pixels per em of the font; VAT may display it as "lem".
By default font size (relative): each unit equals to the size of the default font; VAT may display it as "rem".
By a half of default font size (relative): each unit equals to a half of the size of the default font; VAT may display it as "ren".
By viewport width (relative): each unit equals to the width of the window viewport; VAT may display it as "vw".
By viewport height (relative): each unit equals to the height of the window viewport; VAT may display it as "vh".
By parent container width (relative): each unit equals to the width of the parent Container of the Component; VAT may display it as "cw".
By parent container height (relative): each unit equals to the height of the parent Container of the Component; VAT may display it as "ch".
By reference container width (relative): each unit equals to the width of the reference Container of the Component, only when defined; VAT may display it as "rw".
By reference container height (relative): each unit equals to the height of the reference Container of the Component, only when defined; VAT may display it as "rh".
By screen pixel (absolute): each unit equals to a screen pixel of the current display; VAT may display it as "spx".
By logical pixel (absolute): each unit equals to a logical pixel on the screen without influence of scale; VAT may display it as "lpx".

content.p: For Rational Units for Numeric Values, maybe some factors are accessible as constants or variables with numerical calculations instead of being a dedicated unit. There may be a screen scale factor, where each unit equals to a scale factor of the screen device; VAT may display it as "ss".

Colors may be in various formats, but there shall not be preset colors; such may be provided and aided by a VAT. There may be variants for color spaces, algorithms, and numeric formats. For example, percentage for linear RGB, 8-bit sRGB, HSL, Display P3, CIELAB color spaces. Resultant colors must resemble as the closest as possible as defined in the color space if the values lie outside the device gamut.
Colors filters (from different ancestors) on a Component must be summarized into a single filter when rendering a graphics within the Component.

For cases when author settings specified invalid combinations of values, errors or warnings shall be emitted whenever each one is discovered via certain algorithms. This includes when layout values are "over-constrained", that the combination of values mismatches the expected valid range of configuration, by configurations from ancestors or elsewhere.

If some attributes like maximum or minimum values exist, there might be modes selectable. For example, priorities of those value constrains when computations lie in, like how it should magnify or diminish depending on situations. However, if something has intrinsic ratios, it would not be as simple as just having maximum/minimum width/height to compute using intrinsic ratios, as the algorithm used in CSS is too specific and unparameterized (too much constrains and may not be too useful, and there is fixed preference of order of processing of attributes; specifically it may be problematic to just have two separate different attributes for attribute superseding, but having a mode of algorithm or the like, so object-fit may be taken as a reference in this case).

It is quite possible that conditions of invalid configurations cannot be determined during analysis time, but only determined during layout computations. For such situation, if there is a possibility that configurations may be valid but attribute conditions vary, analysis time validation shall be skipped for possible false positives. When there is undetermined values during computation times, errors shall be thrown, or else in compatibility mode, warnings may be logged. Thus, it is possible that for some attributes, if authors are confident that such undetermined condition must not occur, certain values could be set to undetermined/unimplemented but errors must be thrown in strict mode if it is reached in any way. There is also a possibility for some situations, environment conditions are not enough to trigger invalid configurations.

In order to log useful information, layout states may be recorded or printed for debugging of errors if debugging mode is enabled in strict mode. It might not be too useful in compatibility mode though, and possibly that debugging mode cannot be implemented well in compatibility mode.

Certain layouts provide methods to position components by offsets. The relative offsets are defined by anchors, where there are a host anchor that is a chosen anchor in the subject, and a target anchor that is a chosen anchor in the reference object. A reference object could be its direct parent Container, or several levels of Container, or specific reference point like how Selector works, or its absolute Container (either Screen/Menu).

A Containing Block/Box is the Content Box of a box's direct parent Container. A Visual Block includes background, border area, border box and any content. A Layout Box includes margin box, etc. (Those terminologies are actually not used below.)

(Tentative Proposal) Not every Layout allows margins. Each margin edge may specify clearance that may never be collapsed with clearance regions of other margins. Only non-clearance margin regions may collapse. Clearance breadth must be equal or less than total margin breadth. (Another Proposal) Instead of dedicated margins, just make everything Containers, and having a Layout in a Component to pad its Contents itself. (Roles of Margins) If positioning ability is enough, there is no need to implement something like Margins at all. Margins have nothing to do with actual contents, even visible. If Margin is not implemented, use cases should be possible to be replaced with Paddings of Container or gaps between Objects set by a Layout, or even just various positioning attributes. If no Margins, no need to consider collapsing Margins.

If a Layout supports padding, borders, and potentially margins, those properties can be set for a Facet. A Facet of a Layout is a part or a feature in a Layout, like in Border Layout, if there is a center element, the center element can be a specific Facet defined.

Overflowing is prohibited, but other features shall be utilized. Note that Contents shall never exceed its Component's boundaries, and thus shall always be hidden. Scrolling mechanisms shall only be provided via special Panes, including whether to provide scrollbars.

For Box Dimensions, it is common for Containers to adjust dimensions to fit their Contents, so there may be several factors for a Box to construct dimensions. Occasionally, dimensions of Boxes may affect positioning of other Contents. It is also possible when configurations of factors result in undefined behaviors or cyclic relationships, where a dimension may be a factor of another dimension.

Text must be rendered in lines for generally formatted contents, except for those designed and laid out specifically for certain Layouts. Occasionally, there may be just one line of text, but such cases still follow the general rules for text rendering. Each new style context may form a dedicated em-box (maybe another term). For line height, the height must be the minimal height that can just fit all em-boxes in such line with baseline alignment. Text vertical alignment cannot be changed, but special styles like superscripts and subscripts may vary, so a generalized behavior must be confirmed.

For optimization of line calculations and styles, there must be a primitive class for a text line that is usable for simple text content. Such content contain almost only simple style information usable for variety of usages, to provide supports for displaying computed contents from advanced text contents. However, for several situations including even the simplest situation where the parent container includes just the simple line, there shall (or may) be text style/layout context, including struts.
Styles that alter text contents shall not be implemented in ASD to reduce complexity, including text indentation and text transform.
When a depender takes attributes of a dependee as parameters, a dependency dynamic formatting is formed.

Certain attributes may have ranges that depender may accept initially to reduce unnecessary recomputations. For example, if certain layouts requires a minimal space for another thing to be laid out and the minimal value of the range exceeds that, such condition could be predicted in advance.
It is also possible for several Components being juxtaposed with some or all of them dynamically adjusted according to each other or total spacing of the area.
Cyclic dependencies cause errors in formatting and shall not proceed further.
No negative values are accepted in spacing and dimensions. Dimensions likely only accept positive values. Positions likely sometimes constrained by special ranges.

A LayoutManager should include a LayoutViewport. AGIMOs should include a LayoutHandle (read-only) representative of the AGIMO in the Layout Viewport. A LayoutHandle should include all data involved with this particular, including a reference to containing block, boxes and positions. A Container's Content Box shall be the Containing Block of descendant Components.

All Components are block-level in CSS's sense, inline elements do not exist in AGIM System, but in another form in text formatting models. Components are not free to configure Display modes, but shall be constrained in certain ways. CSS Floats are likely impossible in current proposals of ASD; there is no "inline" element in AGIM/ASD, so there is no point to implement floats from CSS.

Flow in CSS can be explained by Layout in AGIM and ASD. Within a Layout, managed Components must not overlap each other within AGIM System. Although the original draft is derived from CSS specs, there is no intention to resemble most behaviors of CSS.

There is nothing called "generated content" in ASD but rather possibly generation algorithms of contents provided as functions for Authors in Kyon. Resolve issue about having counters as parts of styles of listing while keeping principal of preserving all controls in Kyon: this includes "content" and list styles per CSS; it is quite complicated to implement this in ASD. Also implementing counters in ASD seems not too aesthetic in specification. It is possible that specific styles of counters being fully controlled in Kyon but ASD can define or change the styles of said counters, though specific counting and usages of counters shall still be in Kyon. The box of the list markers must be constrained and controlled within AGIMO as a part of an AGIMO, so the marker itself is a Component, but whether it should be a part of a list item object or entry or a part of the entire list, still yet to be considered. Thus, the presence and primary styles of a marker must be defined within Kyon.

States of Cursor must be defined in ASD, but this may be either system cursor or custom cursor. In the case of system cursor, there may be about a dozen of preset depending on platforms, and some platforms may support using custom cursor images. Or otherwise, system cursor shall be hidden for the appearance of custom cursor in application. It is a question whether to use system cursors by default, or implement own custom cursors instead. For custom cursors, maybe both vector (SVG) and bitmap (CUR, ICO, etc.) cursors can be supported; certain formats require hotspots to be defined separately, in ASD attribute.

System colors are not used in application, but in certain cases, if some attributes are resolved in a way platform-specific, there should be a way to determine availability for conditional values and fallbacks, other than implementing hardcoded default values. Likewise, system fonts are also not used, as system fonts commonly vary significantly, authors may use provided fonts in/to application.

Outline may/might be implemented besides occasional available implementation of borders, but might only be implemented with focus/active states. Outlines are rendered as the same shape as borders, with enclosed shapes as defined in CSS. may be either rendered from the position of border edge (outward) or padding edge (inward). Always rendered on top of an AGIMO, but can be overlayed by other AGIMOs
Tables are likely implemented through Panes with Grid Layout or Table Layout. Only Position Layout allows setting position relative to an anchor configured.

If a Layout is determined that bidirectionality may be effective in the Layout definition and structure, one may apply the effect of bidirectionality. Examples include list items, table columns, flex boxes, etc. Writing directions and text bidirectionality may have different effects depending on investigations. Most likely, when a text content is internationalized, its bidirectionality shall respect the attribute of the selected language, meaning treating as if a character of RLI or LRI is inserted in the beginning, but likely mixed international texts (not sure whether exists) may generalize this algorithm better. If certainly something is designed to be potentially affected by writing or text direction, those attributes must either be or not be including such factors for computing of said attributes.

for example, when there is are attributes called "left" and "right", those are likely unaffected by direction settings, but attributes like "inline-start" and "inline-end" would be affected in the aspect of resultant layout.

Layout design principles include: Author of contents must specify specific layout for intentional attributes and behaviors. Layouts must avoid implications to certain layout configurations while providing clear guidance and intentions for such layouts, so basically, values like "defaults" or "auto" (as abstract ideas taken from CSS) may have to be avoided.
Usually when authors are choosing a layout, authors are likely given a certain extent of freedom in selection of algorithms and configurations despite limitations of attributes.

Scrolling ability must be provided by ScrollPane with optional ScrollBar configured in the ScrollPane. The Scroll Bar pads a space in the Scroll Pane with any side. The styles of Scroll Bar can inherit from either the contents of the Scroll Pane or its parent. Support up to at most two axial directions of scrolling (either or both horizontal and vertical). Scroll bars can be chosen to be hidden when there is no scrolling needed.

NavigationHelper (or something another better name) can be a superclass of ScrollPane. This provides utilities to support mechanisms like scrolling including but not limited to scroll bars. Possible configurations include using a panner (panorama). Possibly merge this into Scroll Pane, considering what scrolling actually means. Should consider where there should be customizable styles like borders for Scroll Pane. However, certain options like whether there should be a specific bar in a specific axis (except for conditional hiding which should be in ASD) shall be in sole controls of AGIMO (i.e. Kyon), and cannot be controlled in ASD.

There are two Layouts: (Integrated) Table Layout and Grid Layout. In Table Layout, all cells do not have their own styles but managed via the Layout. In Grid Layout, every grid cell is independently managed and styled, but overall styles are managed by the Layout. There shall be a common superclass Matrix Layout.

In Matrix Layout: Either a number of rows or a number of columns must be specified. If both are specified, excessive cells result in errors. If there is a row or a column is not fully filled, either warning or error shall be emitted, since this usually causes unsatisfactory experience. Priorities of rows and columns are as balanced as possible, so resolutions may always be used when collisions between specifiers to rows and columns occur. Direction (both row/column but row/column must be horizontal/vertical) may be specified in either Layout or ASD (not decided). Cells are stored in linked lists in both forms of rows and columns, with indices. A cell may span a number of rows and/or columns, specified in Layout, and thus rectangular. Thus, two kinds of indices are made for each cell (or list node): by atomic index (index of the unit cells) and by elemental index (index of the spanned cells). It should be preferred that cells should not be updated during rendering of layouts to reduce insertions of cells and computations of lists. However, overlapped cells result in errors whenever occurred. Most of the time, max/min width/height would be set for columns and rows, but if constraints conflict, errors shall be emitted during layout process. Each cell then lays out according to computed dimensions, but it is possible that dimensions of Matrix depend fully on content dimensions computed for individual cells. However, if the dimensions of Matrix depend on its Container, cells shall be justified for the dimensions or errors shall be thrown if the dimensions cannot be fully justified. Usually follow the general algorithm for unconstrained layouts.

In Table Layout: To simplify structures, caption(s) of a Table must be made in a Layout that includes the Table, like a Flexbox can include a caption and a Table. Any rows and columns can be specified as headers but must be in rows and/or columns; likewise, the same for footers. Only when row specifiers and column specifiers are defined in Layout, styles for those could be specified in ASD. Certain properties like background and styles can be applied by rows and columns, but when there is a possibility that a cell may be styled by both a row specifier and a column specifier, a resolution function (or in ASD?) must be supplied or an error shall be thrown. Common specifier (including row, column or whole):

list.li: background, text styles, borders, visibility (collapsing; only applicable to non-whole specifier)

collapsing is by groups of rows or columns, with priority
collapsed cells are still in Layout and must not be excluded from computations, but sizes of Table may be either justified or unchanged from collapsed cells
may specify how the state of collapsing is changed by user control or whatever, so this attribute must be specified in Kotlin

content.p: Row specifier: min/max height OR fixed height. Column specifier: min/max width OR fixed width. When height and width are both specified for a cell, a resolution to unconstraint a dimension or clipping must be specified.
In Grid Layout: Styles can only be specified to whole (compared with Table). Gaps may be specified vertically, horizontally or both, but must be explicitly set.
(Tentative Proposal; incomplete) General Content Layout Algorithm (as entry):

list.li: Note: there is a constraint influenced by the Container on a dimension of this box if and only if the dimension of the Container does not depend on this dimension.
Note: a fixed constraint means that the constraint only accepts a single value rather than a range.

Note: if there are several constraints with different values on the same property and there is no overlap with all those constraints, errors shall be emitted.
In compatibility mode, usually this would be resolved with the smallest value with warnings emitted.
Note: a constraint can be influenced by the box's Container or a set attribute on the box.

For each dimension:
If there is a fixed constraint on this dimension, mark this dimension as fixed with the value.
Otherwise:
If there is an intrinsic value or a set fixed length for this dimension, let it be the desired length (DL). Or otherwise, compute DL for this dimension by the General Unconstrained Dimension Algorithm.
If there is one or more constraint (range(s)) on this dimension:
Compute the overall constraint (OC), a range, from the constraint(s).
If DL is smaller than OC, mark this dimension as relaxed with the minimal value of OC.
Otherwise, if DL is greater than OC, mark this dimension as constrained with the maximal value of OC.
Otherwise, mark this dimension as fit with the value of DL.
Otherwise, mark this dimension as fit with the value of DL.

Note: at the moment, those enums have the same meanings.
fixed, constrained: following is simplified as fixed
But with constrained, this usually means the dimension is in excess if DL for this is a set value than a computed value.
relaxed, fit: following is simplified as fit
If there is a dimension marked as fixed, apply the computed tentative dimensions to the General Constrained Layout Algorithm.
Otherwise, apply the computed tentative dimensions to the General Unconstrained Layout Algorithm.

content.p: When implementing major features, make sure those use cases where anyway possible in this architecture or framework, may be effective. Those include:

list.li: direct reference to another attribute in several modes; could be of the same Object

computations in attributes:
using other similar attribute values (either static (same context; likely acting like constant) or dynamic (maybe updated or superseded by others)) as arguments or operators to compute value(s) for such attribute.
calculating maximum or minimum width/height by a relative value like a percentage of another width/height attribute, potentially with an offset or something.

(possibly) reproduce abilities of Margins from CSS, in this framework of ASD solely by utilizing all available features, for any use cases with same exact or similar (but with the same exact intentions and objectives) behaviors.

content.p: For non-OpenGL backends, wgpu library shall be leveraged as an abstract interface over other various lower-level backends. For OpenGL, glow shall be used as the support of OpenGL in wgpu is not optimal to our requirements, while a separate abstraction layer is strictly required. Since in recent versions of wgpu, support for Direct3D 11 has been removed, it is necessary to implement our own backend for Direct3D 11 via d3d11 helper with required traits exposed in wgpu-hal. Any chance if wgpu is not compatible with D3D 11 during development, another backend abstraction besides wgpu shall be implemented; this is possible due to the fact that D3D 11 is higher level than D3D 12. When one backend is chosen, a specific implementation with a chosen backend shall be used, with all abstractions handled using traits and implemented structs.

Abstraction layer with OpenGL is sophisticated as different version provide different features, and when certain important extensions are available, those extension functions shall be used. Like wgpu abstraction, there shall also be an abstraction with OpenGL across different states of OpenGL features, so various traits for different situations may be handled. For example, in a major handle of OpenGL, separate modules as dynamic traits for various features like VAO and UBO handling shall be implemented in their own implementations, where during initialization of handle, suitable implementations shall be chosen for each feature.

On GUI, the camera is fixed, so the view is also fixed and constant. Therefore, in shaders, the view matrix and transformation are omitted and disregarded. The projection should always be orthogonal and thus being a uniform value, while the model transformation and color filter would be done per instance as uniform values evaluated each frame depending on the specifics, but not per vertex.

There would be several sets of texture atlases implemented in the Engine. Texture atlases should be used to enhance performance since there would mostly be a large number of texture units used in the game; otherwise frequent texture bindings which are likely expensive operations may occur. In general, one might use half pixel correction to solve the issue, but the outcome may not be ideal or fit perfectly with the rendering results due to the clipped outermost pixels in a tile as a texture atlas element (later referred as "texel"). Therefore, it is more recommended to have paddings or border pixels for each texel in an atlas to keep the outermost pixels rendered well. Even using "nearest neighbor" filters without paddings may not help solve the issue completely because of potential numeric rounding errors. All GUI textures would be managed with an atlas without any mipmapping, while all tile, item and entity textures would be managed with different atlases with mipmapping.

Different textures would have different constrains resulting different configurations. Since GUI textures are not supposed to be scaled down, but scaled up depending on the scaling setting with the base layout set based on the lowest reference scaling, mipmapping is not suitable for this. On the other hand, the gameplay region may be scaled up or down, so mipmapping may be applied to enhance the performance of rendering diminished textures. Regardless of whether the atlas would be mipmapped, paddings would be done by repeating the outermost pixels to the desired extent for each texel. However, when the atlas is mipmapped, the padding size would be the number of pixels by two to the power of the maximum mipmap level with the atlas, so paddings still take effect for each mipmap. When the atlas reached the hardware-limited size (known by GL_MAX_TEXTURE_SIZE), a new atlas for the same configurations should be used, but stored together in a managed set. Also, manual mipmapping for each texel is required to avoid edge bleeding during mipmapping; computations of texture atlases would be performed and designed with reference to
the rectangle packing algorithm by David Colson or crates like rectangle-pack and crunch-rs; unless the texels are explicitly constrained to only powers of two, this kind of advanced algorithm would still be used.

In general, since the art style tends to be pixelated, mostly "nearest neighbor" would be used to magnify the texels, but blending would be applied for diminishing to simulate the similar colors. At least, the mipmaps would be weighted using linear interpolation, but color filtering could be either one of the available options through settings or launching options due to rendering quality and computational complexity. The maximum mipmapping level would be determined by the greatest power of two from the common factors of all texel dimensions in the specific atlas, for which could be further limited through settings or launching options. Basically, there would still be the enforced constraint to the maximum value like four; the dimensions of tile texels and that of entity texels must be a multiple of 8 and 2 respectively.

Besides, the application would first enter the early loading stage to render the progress by initializing minimal components required to show the progress bar and the loading screen. So, the logo used in the loading screen would be embedded in the application, and other components would be started loading and tracked after the initialization of the screen. The loading screen may also show during loading of updated resource pack configurations. Moreover, a short animated splashscreen could show before the loading screen.

Any GMO would internally hold an opaque handle managed by the Engine. When a Screen is sent to the active stack, the handle in the Engine would be sent to the internally held state, RenderingState, to be used during rendering. The state internally holds an empty Mutex lock which controls which thread to allow access to only one thread for thread-safety. Ideally, only the GMS ticking thread and the main thread, which performs rendering, would access the state either for modifications or reading for rendering. The state impacts the thread for modifications only when the GMOs are within the state, where the state would internally mark it during transitions. This pipeline could greatly reduce JNI calls during rendering to improve performance with only one call per loop as the general ideas. Note that synchronization must be carefully examined for any data accessed in the Engine.

In general, rendering of any GMO should avoid reading framebuffer data drawn by any previous GMO in the rendering loop. This includes applying visual effects like color inverting or copying; this is due to parallelization of shader computations in the render devices. (See the related question.) Various optimizations are also conducted, like reusing same shader programs as much as possible when the previous draw call was also using the same program, eliminating unnecessary OpenGL commands.

Basically, an audio mixing public interface may be implemented for usages by other modules. It should also provide various configurations in preferences for the exact controls over mixing, like using software mixers or native sound cards directly, or even setting equalizers or compressors. Modules may also add other mixers for other usages, or even using external software.
Across the application, there shall be a top-level generic manager of audio. In the scope of gameplay, there should be another subsystem of gameplay audio as another manager under the top-level one.

In terms of modularization, with the MUI structure, different components could be placed and organized optimally. Besides, the components less related to UI-oriented functions could be separated from the MUI modules. In Kotlin, those "modules" may be Java packages instead.

For example, interfaces of input devices could be put into a KUI module and inner details of the devices could be put into a HID module under a possibly I/O module. At the same time, more sophisticated UI components could be put into submodules of their UI modules, like detailed rendering functions could be put into a graphics (GFX) module under the GUI module, though they may be too deep into implementation details to be inside the GUI module.

On Windows, DirectX may be preferred over other backends for optimal performance and support. However, due to complexities of supports across different versions, only DirectX 11 and 12 shall be supported, while the later shall be used over the former when available. This is especially important on older platforms of Windows 7/8/Vista or when support of Direct3D 12 is problematic, that a fallback to an alternative may be required.

Information about DirectX can be fetched in the way as in
a sample usage . This includes DirectX versions and all required features in DirectX. When DirectX 12 is not available, DirectX 11 may be used if available. When DirectX 12 is available, DirectX 11 should also be available. If both of them are not available, the ability to choose DirectX as backend is disabled. However, if one or more of them are available, abilities to choose them should be available. It is suggested to use DirectX on Windows when a backend is not specified.

As a general idea, the minimal support version is OpenGL 2.0. Although at the time this is written, most consumer devices in the last decade should support OpenGL 3.0 and above, 2.0 is still targeted as the minimal version for most other potential users. However, when a newer version or usable extension is detected with the OpenGL context, advanced features that may improve performance or even other effects might be available.
In versions prior than 3.0, an extension of GL_ARB_vertex_array_object may be required for VAOs. Otherwise, manual bindings to objects shall be implemented.
In versions prior than 3.1, an extension of GL_ARB_uniform_buffer_object may be required for UBOs. Otherwise, regular uniforms shall be used instead.

According to Wikipedia, the GLSL version in OpenGL 2.0 is 1.10, so version 110 would be used as the base GLSL version to use for all the shaders used in the Engine. If a more advanced GLSL version is supported while advanced features are used, the target GLSL version should be specified and the shaders are applied only when the target version is matched for both GL and GLSL versions. This is said, some shaders might be used or available only when they are available provided by the OpenGL context.
